Daily Digest Tuesday, July 14, 2026

GPT-5.6 Drops in Three Tiers, Starbucks Ditches Enterprise Software, AI SDR Workflows Cut Costs 38%

GPT-5.6 launches with Sol/Terra/Luna tiers. Starbucks ditches enterprise software for homegrown AI. AI-assisted SDR workflows cut cost-per-lead by 38%.

  1. 1

    OpenAI Releases GPT-5.6 with Sol, Terra, Luna Tiers

    After a White House cybersecurity delay, OpenAI shipped GPT-5.6 to the public with three distinct capability tiers: Sol (highest), Terra, and Luna. Alongside it, the new ChatGPT Work agent can run multi-app projects for hours without supervision. For PMM teams, this is a signal that AI "coworkers" capable of sustained execution — not just quick answers — are entering production.

    Read on Anicca ↗
  2. 2

    Starbucks Building In-House AI to Cut $400M in Software Spend

    Starbucks is developing homegrown AI-powered tools to replace Microsoft inventory systems and IBM maintenance platforms — aiming to slash $400M in annual software costs. This is either visionary cost-cutting or a case study in corporate hubris. The real question for enterprise software vendors: when AI makes "build vs. buy" tilts toward build, what happens to your TAM?

    Read on Motley Fool ↗
  3. 3

    Salesforce: AI-Assisted SDR Workflows = 38% Drop in Cost-Per-Lead

    Salesforce's 2026 State of Marketing research found B2B teams running AI-assisted SDR or content workflows saw a 38% drop in cost-per-lead alongside more meetings booked per rep. This is where AI is genuinely paying off — not in generating more content, but in automating the repetitive outreach that burns SDR time.

    Read on Big News Network ↗
  4. 4

    Deloitte: 80% Confident in AI, 75% Say Operating Models Must Change

    Deloitte's 2026 Global Technology Leadership Study reveals a paradox: over 80% of senior IT executives are confident in their ability to deploy and govern AI at scale, but 75% believe operating models and business processes must change substantially in the next 12-18 months. The implication for marketers: your AI use cases will increasingly need governance documentation. Start building that muscle now.

  5. 5

    MarTech's Shift: From Demographics to AI-Driven Intent Modeling

    MarTech Series makes the case that the future of marketing isn't knowing who customers are — it's predicting what they'll do next. Modern AI models analyze millions of interactions to identify buying signals far earlier than traditional methods. The shift from targeting demographics to orchestrating intent-based experiences is reshaping how MarTech platforms justify their value. Read this one: The Starbucks story. When a company with Starbucks' scale decides to build rather than buy enterprise software, it's a warning shot at the entire SaaS industry. AI is making internal development faster and cheaper — and that changes the math on every "land and expand" motion in enterprise sales. If you're marketing enterprise software, this is the trend to watch.
